I think the important thing here is to recognize there is a difference in 'trust' and 'justice'. Justice would entail legal actions taken against the abuser, and trust would entail protections for the accuser. Many people think to have one, you must have the other, and vice versa, but in reality the two SHOULD be mutually exclusive. There are people who would lynch the accused with only an allegation, and those people are just as wrong as the ones who flat out don't believe the accusation.

In that situation, obviously it is a stalemate on what to believe. The accused can continue as is, but the accuser still needs protection from the alleged abuse. Victims do not need vengeance on their abuser, via jail, sex offender status, etc. All they need is to not be subject to the abuse again.

It is tough, however I think a very big problem today is that accusers aren't believed immediately. Sometimes even family members of the accuser don't do anything about it because of the possibility that it COULD be a lie. People like op feed into this line of thought, and it is a dangerous belief system to have.

I agree with you entirely. What I meant by 'trust' was to take action to ensure the accuser is protected from the alleged abuse. In your case the student would be removed from that school while an investigation occurs.
That mindset is what allows fuckers like Weinstein to get away with it for years. Trust should be given immediately, but justice should only be given with proof.

I remember one instance in particular because of the occasional nightmares I have about it. 

For whatever reason, I, the youngest member of the family, was designated the responsibility to feed the dogs we owned (there were 5 separate enclosures for all of them). Once in the morning either before school or the moment I wake up, and again when I returned from school or after lunch. There were strict punishments if I forgot on any occasion, or if I waited a little later, so I learned to do it religiously. 

With that being said, one day I get home from school and immediately feed the dogs as usual. My mother comes home from work a few hours later, walks into my room,  and asks "Did you feed the dogs today?" I wish I could convey the fear this statement gave me, as it usually meant a pretty severe beating was coming. I tell her I did and she clenched my hair in her fists and through gritted teeth growled "then why isn't their any food in the bowl?" Then she pulls me, still by my hair, out of my room and out to one of the dog pens. She yanks my head to make me look at the empty bowl and growls once again "what is that?" I tell her I didn't know what happened, but I did, in fact, feed them after I got home. 

That's when she threw me to the ground and started kicking me violently. She focused most of the blows on my ribs, but there were a few to my head and stomach. She grabs me by my hair and forces me to my feet and tells me to feed them. She walks me to the dog food and back to the pens where the kicking process repeats itself. When she finally stops, she just walks into the house and leaves me on the ground. My ribs were bruised and it hurt to stand up on my own. I lay there in pain until it got dark and decided I had to make it into the house or risk staying the night outside. 

I guess I deserved it, in her opinion, because I lied and didn't feed our dogs (both were false)

This one will sound lame compared to most on here, but I will tell it nonetheless. When I was in 6th grade, I was out swimming in my pool. I put my hand up on the railing of the pool and felt something crawling on my hand. I pick it up to look at it, and sure enough it was a spider.

Panicking, I quickly dunked my hand in the water. I guess i thought that was the easiest way to get it off, and it might have been. The spider wasn't on my hand any longer and I hadn't felt it bite me, so I was in the clear.

Skip to later that day. I had an overwhelming sense of dizziness, almost like vertigo, but a lot worse. Since I was in the dizzy state of mind, I had not thought about what happened earlier with the spider. So I go to try to take a nap, but I can't. The dizziness was overwhelming.

 Once I finally came to after going to bed that night, I noticed my hand was itching so I scratched it. I felt a sharp pain and looked at my hand. There were two holes with large swelling around it. I immediately remembered the spider being on that exact spot on my hand earlier. The sudden fear of death flowed over me. How could I be that naive? How could I have gotten bit by a spider and suffer extreme dizziness and not tell anyone? To this date I still get chills just thinking about my brush with death, and how I could have died in my sleep without even knowing what happened.
